🔻 Armed Forces chief stresses domestic capabilities to strengthen electronic, cyber warfare

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Chief of Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces Major General Ali Abdollahi has stressed the need to rely on domestic capabilities and the country’s elite youth to boost air defense’s electronic and cyber warfare capabilities.

In a message to the commander of Iran’s Air Defense Force on the occasion of Air Defense Day, Major General Abdollahi congratulated the force’s personnel and highlighted the key expectations outlined in the appointment decree of martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.
​
He described those expectations as a clear roadmap for the transformation and advancement of the strategic force, particularly amid the current critical circumstances facing Iran.
​
The top general said Iran is currently facing the “third imposed American-Zionist war,” adding that the country’s defense strategy should focus on offensive defense capabilities and the creation of an integrated, active, dynamic and preemptive air defense network.
​
Major General Abdollahi also stressed the need to connect all reconnaissance, radar and missile layers through an intelligent and resilient network capable of intercepting and neutralizing potential threats at the greatest possible distance.
​
He further called for the localization and smartification of defense systems through the development of advanced technologies and the deployment of systems designed specifically for electronic and cyber warfare.
​
“Reliance on domestic capabilities and elite young people” is essential to enhancing the Air Defense Force’s electronic and cyber warfare capabilities, the commander said.
​
He also called for greater synergy with other branches of the Armed Forces as part of the General Staff’s broader strategy to provide a “timely, revolutionary and effective response” to any level or conventional or modern military, cognitive or hybrid threat against the Islamic Republic.

🖥 Shanghai Plus countries can help build multipolar world, Iranian President says

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has told member states, observers and partners of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization under the Shanghai Plus framework that they can play an important role in building a multipolar world based on multilateralism, sovereign equality and the rule of law.

Addressing a summit of Shanghai Plus countries, Pezeshkian called for more equitable and effective action by the United Nations and its Security Council in dealing with global developments.
​
He said changes in the international balance of power should not result in one center of power being replaced by another or in the transfer of hegemony.
​
Pezeshkian said the United Nations should better represent the realities of the changing world and more effectively fulfill its mission of maintaining international peace and security, preventing war and peacefully resolving disputes.
​
In this context, he described the performance of the United Nations and the Security Council in dealing with developments in Gaza, Lebanon and the recent aggression against Iran as “very disappointing.”
​
The Iranian president also said attacks by the United States and the Israeli regime against Iran, including attacks on civilian centers, vital infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities, constituted clear violations of the UN Charter and principles of international law.
​
He said the continuation of such actions could undermine countries’ confidence in international mechanisms and diplomacy.
​
At the same time, Pezeshkian said diplomacy and negotiations remained the main path for resolving disputes and stressed the need for good faith, respect for commitments and avoidance of the use of force to achieve lasting peace.
​
The full text of his speech follows:
​
In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful
​
His Excellency Mr. Japarov, esteemed President of the Kyrgyz Republic;
​
Esteemed Secretary-General of the United Nations;
​
Esteemed Secretary-General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization;
​
Excellencies, distinguished heads of state and government;
​
At the outset, I would like to congratulate the Kyrgyz Republic on its Independence Day and sincerely thank His Excellency Mr. Japarov, the esteemed President of the Kyrgyz Republic, as well as the government and people of this country for their worthy hosting of this meeting and their valuable efforts during their chairmanship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.
​
I also welcome the presence of the organization’s member states, observers and partners under the Shanghai Plus framework.
​
With its geographical reach and political and economic capacities, this framework can become one of the important platforms for dialogue and cooperation among countries playing an effective role in shaping the future international order.
​
Today’s topic of discussion, namely the role of the United Nations as a fundamental pillar of a just global order and the contribution of Shanghai Plus countries to achieving a multipolar world, confronts us with a fundamental question.
​
The distribution of economic, political and technological power is evolving.
​
More countries seek to play a more effective role in international decision-making, and the new realities of the international system no longer fully correspond to structures formed in past decades.
​
But the fundamental question is how this transformation should be managed.
​
From the perspective of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the answer should not be sought in replacing one center of power with another.
​
The goal should not be the transfer of hegemony from one power to anot . . .
